newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile to study private capital for Enami - Frei.
newsitem.headline: Chile to study private capital for Enami - Frei.

text.p: Chile's government will study ways to bring private investment to state copper processing company Empresa Nacional de Mineria (Enami) and possibly into a state oil company, President Eduardo Frei said.
Frei, speaking in his annual speech to Congress, said Enami and state oil company Empresa Nacional del Petroleo, or Enap, need to modernize and adapt to changing market realities.
But he made no concrete announcements of privatizations or alliances with private concerns at either company, despite expectations by some local media.

Enami's own modernization efforts at its smelter at Paipote and smelter and refinery in Ventanas would not be enough to make the company competitive, which will take capital from "third parties," said Frei.

"Today we are investing in the modernization of Ventanas and Paipote, with special emphasis on projects that allow us to reduce their environmental impact," he said. "But we know this effort won't be enough. We must study ways to incorporate capital from third parties into those installations as the only way of guaranteeing their medium and long-term competitiveness."
He suggested that Enami's unions, known for their propensity to strike, and management should reach agreement on how to proceed.

"Enap and Enami are companies with a future. We call on their executives and workers to build a common project to consolidate that future. This is an indispensable condition to guarantee the efficiency and competitiveness of state companies," said Frei.
Both companies faced "the threat of decadence and failure" if they did not modernize and grow, he said.

On Enap, Frei said his government was working on "a medium-term strategic plan...contemplating various investment alternatives, whose financing could require the incorporation of third-party capital into the company if its own readily-available funds...are not sufficient," said Frei.
Government sources have said the government plans to sell controlling stakes in two oil refineries owned by Enap, one at Concon and the other in Concepcion.
Unions have opposed the plan, and on Tuesday unionsat Enami's Ventanas plant staged a two-hour strike to protest against any thought of privatizing any part of Enami or Enap.

Chilean media have reported that a special government commission has recommended selling controlling stakes in both of Enami's main plants plus two smaller processing plants as a way of repaying Enami's heavy debts.
